section.title: 对话 1
section.preview: I'm going to the city center to buy a new phone today.

lines.text: I'm going to the city center to buy a new phone today.
Didn't you buy a new phone just two months ago?
It was three months ago,
and I already know what you're going to say.
You're thinking I shouldn't replace my phone this soon.
No, actually, I was wondering how you could possibly afford a new phone.
But now that you mention it,
I do think getting another phone so soon is wasteful,
regardless of the cost.
Maybe you're right.
But the thing is,
everyone at the office has a nice, expensive phone,
and I'm a little embarrassed by mine.
I just got a credit card,
so I thought I might as well buy a new phone.
I don't think buying a phone on credit is a good idea.
Look, you've only been working for five months now.
People understand that you are a recent graduate,
and I doubt anyone cares about your phone other than yourself.
Maybe you're right,
but the credit card has a very good special offer,
where I don't pay any interest for six months.
I'll be able to pay for the phone well before that period is over.
I still think it's a bad idea to use a credit card for something you don't need.
One of my colleagues bought a lot of things on credit during her first year of work,
and it became a bad habit,
and she accumulated a lot of debt.
Well, I can see how that might happen to someone,
and I'm sure she regrets it,
but I know it won't happen to me.
